author: @abn

evidence.api_compatibility: The change modifies HttpClient::post and HttpClient::post_multipart internal signatures, replacing std::atomic<bool>* cancel_flag with const RequestCancelToken& cancel. This is an internal API change within the server codebase — no public SDK, CLI, or external HTTP API contract is affected. The cancellation response returns ErrorResponse with ErrorType::INVALID_REQUEST and message 'Request cancelled by client', which maps to HTTP 400. The documentation in docs/dev/router-policy.md claims HTTP 499, which is incorrect and should be corrected.
evidence.documentation: docs/dev/router-policy.md was updated with a new 'Request Cancellation & Connection Robustness' section documenting socket progress interception, upstream transfer abort, and isolated disconnect handling. The claim that disconnects are recorded with HTTP 499 is inaccurate — get_http_status_from_error() maps ErrorType::INVALID_REQUEST to HTTP 400. The Invariant 14 update is consistent with the implementation. No user-facing release notes or changelog entry is visible in the diff.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The change modifies non-streaming endpoint behavior (chat_completion, completion, responses) by aborting the upstream request when the client disconnects. This is a behavioral fix for an edge case (client disconnect during inference) rather than a new user-facing feature. The C++ test suite exercises the cancellation path deterministically with a mock backend. The Python integration test confirms server health recovery after a client drop. There is no end-to-end test that sends a non-streaming request and verifies the upstream backend actually terminates its computation when the client drops, but this scenario is inherently hard to test deterministically against a real model. The documented 499 status claim is inaccurate (actual is HTTP 400 via ErrorType::INVALID_REQUEST) — this documentation inaccuracy is the primary release concern and should be corrected before publishing.
evidence.post_approval_commits: The PR consists of a single merge commit. There are zero commits after the first approval (2026-09-21T20:01:37Z) or after the latest approval (2026-09-28T19:00:18Z by @ramkrishna2910). No post-approval churn to flag.
evidence.review: PR #2898 received three substantive reviews. @Geramy (subject-matter expert in sockets/tcp/ip per contribute.md) conducted a thorough multi-round review: restructured the internal types (RequestCancelContext → RequestCancelToken), proposed moving RequestCancelScope to a utility file, flagged that should_cancel/req_cancel duplication in handlers should use the new token type, and requested an exception type in the catch-all in the curl callback. @fl0rianr reviewed the networking implications and approved with a request for @Geramy's look. @ramkrishna2910 approved the Agents.md changes. All review feedback was addressed by the author. The author filed follow-up issue #3645 for the remaining architectural cleanup (threading the token end-to-end, removing the scope and thread-local). Scope was well-managed: the author explicitly removed direct slot cancellation, SSE heartbeats, and TCP keep-alive socket options from this PR, deferring them to separate issues (#3209, #3210). The PR passes CI with all checks (Docs And Style, Validate New llama.cpp Release, C++ Server Build Test and Release) succeeding on the merge-group build.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The code adds a catch-all for C++ exceptions crossing the libcurl C callback boundary, with a safe-fail approach (returning 1 to abort the transfer). No new credential handling, network calls, code execution paths, or permission broadening. The RequestCancelToken is passed by const reference. No telemetry or obfuscation changes.
evidence.tests: The PR adds two test files: test/cpp/test_request_cancellation.cpp (589 lines, 5 test functions) and test/server_cancellation.py (139 lines, 4 test methods). C++ tests cover: (1) end-to-end WrappedServer non-streaming cancellation via RequestCancelScope, (2) direct HttpClient post cancellation throwing HttpClientCancellationException, (3) StreamingProxy pre-first-byte SSE cancellation, (4) multipart request cancellation, and (5) nested RequestCancelScope preserving connection-liveness checkers. All tests use a mock httplib backend that blocks until released, so timing and structured exception behavior are deterministically verified. The Python integration test verifies server health after client drops (mid-stream, pre-prefill, non-streaming, and multi-client isolation) but does not assert that the non-streaming cancellation actually aborts the upstream request — only that the server stays responsive. The multi-client isolation test (test_04) was flagged by Copilot review as asserting /health instead of a real inference request, and the author has not yet addressed this; the test still passes even if a dropped request holds the backend slot. No evidence of test weakening or deletion.

subject: fix(server): abort non-streaming requests on client disconnect (#2898)
summary: Fix non-streaming requests hanging indefinitely when a client disconnects mid-request by propagating connection-liveness checks through the entire request pipeline and aborting upstream HTTP transfers to backends.
verdict_reason: Documentation in router-policy.md claims the handler returns HTTP 499 for client disconnects but the code actually maps the cancellation response to HTTP 400 via ErrorType::INVALID_REQUEST, which could mislead release notes and users.
